title: Context-aware dedupe & automated runbooks for multiregion SLO excursions
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: Reduce noisy paging during SLO excursions that span multiple regions by combining contextual alert deduplication, dynamic circuit-breaker gating, and orchestrated runbook automation that can both remediate common failure classes and suppress cascaded alerts.
motivation: We've seen several incidents in the last 6 months where a regional spike (network flakiness or autoscaling lag) generated hundreds of pages across multiple teams. This creates fatigue and slows remediation. Because Redwood routes requests across regions and model variants, we need signal-aware suppression and safe automated remediations that preserve availability and cost constraints.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Pager volume for multi-region SLO breaches reduced by >=70% for identical root causes (measured over 30d after rollout).
2) Automated runbooks execute non-destructive remediation for the top 4 incident classes with >80% success rate (verified in staging and canary).
3) Circuit-breaker gating prevents 2nd-order failures (eg. cascading token cache thrash) in >=90% of planned chaos tests.
4) Runbook automation is auditable and can be disabled per-customer in Private deployments.
implementation_summary:
We will implement three complementary layers:

1) Contextual Alert Dedupe: build a correlation engine that groups alerts by fingerprint computed from: region, route, model_id, error_class, recent SLO burn-rate slope, and request fingerprint sketch. The engine emits a single high-fidelity page and attaches a list of suppressed alerts to the incident. Dedup window is configurable (default 2 minutes).

2) Dynamic Severity Mapping + Gatekeeper: map SLO burn-rate and error amplification to pager severity. For multi-region incidents, use an escalation gate that waits for either (a) sustained cross-region burn > X for Y seconds OR (b) manual escalation from an on-call within the suppression window. This prevents immediate P0 storming on transient network blips.

3) Automated Runbooks & Safe Remediations: author playbooks that can (a) restart a serving pool, (b) recycle a KV cache shard, (c) flip routing weight away from a region or model variant, and (d) enable progressive load-shedding profiles. Each action is annotated with prechecks, health probes, and automatic rollback. The Runbook Orchestrator runs remediations as step functions and posts progress back to the incident channel.

4) Circuit Breaker Profiles & Load-shedding tiers: introduce per-region and per-route circuit-breaker thresholds tuned to latency distributions and tail SLOs. When a breaker trips we apply graded shedding: soft-degrade (serve shorter completions / lower-k samples), medium (reduce concurrency per-client), hard (route to lower-cost approximate model). Breaker trips are visible in the incident but suppressed as secondary pages unless they persist beyond the gate timeframe.
plan_tiles:
Phase 1 (2w): telemetry and fingerprint prototype; build correlation keys and suppression heuristics.
Phase 2 (3w): implement gatekeeper logic, severity mapping, and testing harness.
Phase 3 (2w): implement automated runbook actions in staging plus audit/eventing.
Phase 4 (1w): canary rollout to internal services, run chaos + synthetic failure suites.
Phase 5 (1w): gradual rollout to hosted API with metrics and dashboards.

Total: 9 weeks of focused SRE+infra work, but MVP for low-risk suppression and one automated restart action by end of cycle.
updates: 2026-02-14: Kickoff sync with SRE, Serving Runtime, and Console teams. Agreed on basic correlation keys and a 2-minute dedupe default.

2026-02-20: Spike complete — prototype correlation engine using streaming fingerprint that combines {region, route, error_class, model_variant} and a 128-bit sketch. Initial dedupe reduces duplicate alerts in replay by ~62%.

2026-02-28: Design review — Circuit-breaker profile schema approved. Decided to expose per-customer override only in Private deployments. Logged decision to require audit trails for automated actions.
2026-03-05: Implemented gatekeeper logic in routing proxy. Gate waits 30s for cross-region sustained burn before escalating. Added telemetry metric slo.burn_window_seconds for analysis.
2026-03-09: First automated runbook implemented: safe restart of a serving pool with health probes and rollback. End-to-end integration test passed in staging (5/5 runs).

2026-03-12: Canary of dedupe + gatekeeper across internal traffic began (10% traffic). Early results: pages reduced 58% for simulated network flakiness; one false-suppress identified and new whitelist rule added.
notes: Decision: Use a tunable dedupe window (default 120s). Lower bound of 30s for latency-sensitive routes.
Trade-off: Aggressive suppression reduces noise but can mask divergent failures; mitigated by the gatekeeper and synthetic checks.
Follow-up: Add UI controls in Console to visualize suppressed alerts and to manually promote a suppressed group into an active incident.
Risk: Automated actions must be rate-limited per-customer and require an audit log; include HSM/KMS-backed signing for Private deployments.
Future: Integrate with Optimize to suggest load-shedding profiles based on model quantization and cost/latency trade-offs.
testing_plan:
- Replay historical incidents (last 6 months) through the correlation engine and measure pages.
- Run chaos tests for: region network partition, model OOM, KV cache corruption, and autoscaler lag.
- Canary actions on internal tenant traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%), with manual kill-switch.
- Post-deploy 30d SLO and pager volume monitoring.
rollback_criteria:
- If missed-severity incidents (suppression hiding P1/P0) occur in canary more than twice in 24 hours, rollback to previous paging policy.
- If automated remediation causes >2x error rate downstream in 1h, disable that runbook step by default.
- Manual override always available in Console.
